title: Existing derived object comparison for a proper modification
statement: Let $Λ$ be a finite commutative ring. Let $π:Y\to X$ be proper [def-weil-proper-morphism], let $j:U\to X$ and $j\prime:U\prime\to Y$ be open immersions [def-weil-open-immersion], and let $h:U\prime\to U$ be an isomorphism such that the square is cartesian [def-pc-fibre-product]. For any sheaf $G$ of $Λ$-modules on the small etale site of $U$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves], there exists an isomorphism $Rπ_*((j\prime_!h^{-1}G)[0])\simeq(j_!G)[0]$ in the unbounded derived category, using [def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero], [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image], and [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. This asserts an object isomorphism, with no assertion about the specific underived adjunction map.

source.place: nonempty_rightDerivedLowerStar_openImmersionLowerShriek_iso, lines 75-135; existing proved source-library theorem for blueprint lem-finrepair-modification-extension-zero

proof.text: Write F=j\prime_!h^{-1}G and M=Rπ_*(F[0]). Let i be the closed complement of j. Proper base change for the finite coefficient ring [thm-weil-pbc-bounded-below], transported to the unbounded category on this bounded-below object by upperStarRightDerivedLowerStarSingleIso, identifies i^{-1}M with the direct image of the restriction of F to the inverse image of the complement. The two ranges are disjoint, by the pullback identity, so this restriction is zero by [lemma-openclosed-vanishing-lowershriek]. Hence i^{-1}M=0.

The open-closed triangle [lem-cbc-open-closed-recollement] now shows that the counit j_!j^{-1}M → M is invertible: its third object is zero. The source-library exists_distTriang_openClosed is the unbounded form used by the already existing proof.

Etale base change [lem-weil-pbc-etale-localization-exchange] identifies j^{-1}M with Rh_*(j\prime^{-1}F[0]). The unit for extension by zero is invertible by [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-unit-iso], so j\prime^{-1}F ≅ h^{-1}G. Since h is an isomorphism, h^{-1} and h_* are exact inverse equivalences and Rh_*(h^{-1}G[0]) ≅ G[0]. Combine this isomorphism with the inverse counit of step 2 and the exactness of j_! to obtain M ≅ (j_!G)[0]. These are exactly the isomorphisms e₁ and the final composite in the existing Lean proof.
